summary: Added Perry Local Schools (Stark County, Ohio): a malware-related cyber incident closed all schools for one day on 16 November; the district reports no evidence personal data was extracted. No other new US incidents found.

Added Michigan State University: it confirmed suspicious activity and a campus-wide password reset on 1 October, and the BYOD group later claimed data on 1.3 million people (unverified). No new closures found elsewhere.
Routine check: no new US incidents found. Vanderbilt's record now notes a proposed class action over the breach and the university's warning that full recovery may take weeks.

Added 1 unconfirmed incident: Interlock claims a data theft at Ridgway School District R-2 in Colorado, with no district confirmation yet. Richmond's record now lists the data types the attackers claim to hold.

Added 2 incidents: Acadia Parish (Louisiana) shut down its systems on 11 November, and Barbour County (West Virginia) cut district internet in late October; classes continued in both. Richmond's record now includes the forensic audit and its scale.

Routine check: no new incidents found. Vanderbilt's main systems and classes were restored by 10 November, and Springfield's record now reflects the district's report naming Interlock and confirming staff SSNs were taken.

Full-year review of 2026: added 32 US incidents going back to January (26 confirmed, 6 unconfirmed attacker claims). The tracker now covers the United States only; 12 international records moved to an archive file.

Added the Frontline Education vendor breach, which exposed school employee records (reported at about 1.3 million people). Richmond Public Schools gained a source reporting its stolen data was posted to the dark web.

Added Spokane Public Schools (Washington), where the district says student and staff data was compromised in a September attack. Vanderbilt now shows a ransomware group's leak-site claim (unverified).
Tracker launched with 26 incidents researched from news reports, breach trackers and school notices.
